extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, insurers), compliance officers, legal/regulatory staff, and policy analysts implementing HHS Section 1557 nondiscrimination requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory text implementing HHS's final Section 1557 nondiscrimination rule, including required notices, trainings, recordkeeping, coordinator designation, PRA/ICR procedures, small-entity analyses, and substantive nondiscrimination standards that covered entities must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training compliance timeline (§92.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must comply with the §92.9 Training requirements by no later than 300 days of effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule allows additional time for covered entities compared to the Proposed Rule; the revised timeline may postpone certain costs but does not change annualized cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training documentation and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must document employee training as required under §92.9(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden assumptions: one employee spends 15 minutes (0.25 hours) to create the sign-up sheet in the first year and one employee spends one hour collecting and storing attendance forms in the first and subsequent years. Cost estimates use mean hourly wage for clerical staff (updated to $19.02) doubled for overhead; labor-cost examples provided (e.g., $12.6 million first year, $10.1 million subsequent years for universe of covered entities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Section 1557 Coordinator (§92.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15 or more employees must designate a section 1557 Coordinator to coordinate efforts to comply with and carry out responsibilities under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated burden for coordination includes 10 hours annually per covered entity to store complaints and associated records; assumption that administrative or clerical personnel perform these functions; wage assumptions and doubled overhead are used in cost estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance of compliance requirement (§92.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 92.5 retains obligations for covered entities to submit an assurance of compliance to the Department (HHS Form 690).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR provides an online portal for attestation; the Department determined this imposes no additional reporting or recordkeeping requirements under the PRA (PRA approval previously obtained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Nondiscrimination (§92.10) — content and combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide a Notice of Nondiscrimination relating to their health programs or activities to beneficiaries and members of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To minimize burden, a covered entity may combine the content of the notice required by §92.10 with notices required under title VI, section 504, title IX, and the Age Act implementing regulations. OCR estimated personnel burden (updated to 1.34 hours/year) and associated labor and materials costs; notice frequency and delivery channels affect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Availability of Language Assistance and Auxiliary Aids (§92.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide a Notice of Availability that, at minimum, states the covered entity provides language assistance services and auxiliary aids and services free of charge in its health programs and activities, in compliance with section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must be provided to beneficiaries and the public, in English and at least the top 15 languages spoken by persons with LEP in the relevant State(s) (including territories), and must be provided in alternate formats for individuals who request auxiliary aids and services to ensure effective communication. Notices are required (1) annually; (2) upon request; (3) at a conspicuous location on the program/activity homepage; and (4) at conspicuous physical locations where the program/activity interacts with the public. OCR provides cost estimates (monthly and annualized) and notes most material costs scale with notice length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision frequency and conspicuity requirements for notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Notice of Nondiscrimination and Notice of Availability must be provided on an annual basis, upon request, on the homepage of the covered entity's health program or activity, and at conspicuous physical locations where the program or activity interacts with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR updated estimated personnel time to 1.34 hours/year and provided estimated labor and material costs; the estimates vary widely depending on prevalence of electronic delivery and volume of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and alternative format requirement for notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices must be provided in English and at least the top 15 languages spoken by persons with limited English proficiency in the State(s) where the covered entity operates, and must be available in alternate formats for individuals requesting auxiliary aids and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to ensure effective communication for beneficiaries with LEP and individuals with disabilities; costs include translation and alternate-format production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping for grievances (§92.8(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are required to store complaints and associated records as part of coordination and compliance efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR estimated 10 hours annually per covered entity for storing complaint records (assumed performed by administrative/clerical staff); updated wage assumptions and cost calculations are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) solicitation criteria for ICRs
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting an information collection request, the PRA requires agencies to solicit comment on four issues: (1) whether the information collection is necessary and useful; (2) accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden; (3) quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (4) recommendations to minimize the information collection burden, including automated techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR described how PRA burden estimates were updated from the NPRM to reflect revised baseline information and provided detailed burden-hour and cost tables for the ICRs related to §§92.5, 92.7, 92.9, 92.10, and 92.11. OCR also noted OMB approval is required before ICRs become effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA burden-estimation metrics and table components
rubrics_metrics.description: PRA burden estimates use metrics such as number of respondents, responses frequency (average), total responses, burden hours per response (average), hourly rate, and total burden cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR provided an example table (Table 1) listing respondents and burden hours/costs for §§92.7 and §§92.10 & 92.11 and used adjusted wage and respondent counts to compute total application burden and cost. These components are the basis for PRA analysis and public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory alternatives evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyzing regulatory alternatives, the Department considered costs to covered entities, benefits to beneficiaries (including access and quality of care), likelihood that beneficiaries would be aware of their civil rights, litigation reduction, and obligations under federal statutes (including religious/conscience laws).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: removing notice requirements would reduce costs but was rejected because it would reduce information available to beneficiaries; requiring notices only at first encounter would lower costs substantially but was rejected for being too narrow; expanding notices to pharmacies would increase beneficiary information but was rejected for imposing undue burden similar to 2016 requirements. Cost/benefit balance, beneficiary access to information, and statutory obligations guided final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act small-entity impact threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR uses a measure of 'significant economic impact' on a substantial number of small entities defined as a change in revenues of more than 3 percent for at least 5 percent of affected small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR performed threshold analysis using total annualized costs divided by estimated number of small entities to assess whether a 3% revenue impact would be exceeded for at least 5% of small entities; conclusion: very few small businesses would have revenues below the implied threshold and thus the rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity classification and estimation heuristics
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR described how it identified and estimated counts of small covered entities using SBA size standards, Census and SUSB data, and employee-count proxies (e.g., physicians and pharmacies with fewer than 20 employees treated as 'small').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: physician practices (NAICS 62111) size standard based on receipts (<$16M) and proxy of <20 employees yielding counts; pharmacies using <20 employees as proxy for <$37.5M receipts; health insurance issuers using a receipts threshold ($47M) and SUSB 2017 revenue distributions to estimate proportion of issuers considered 'small' (assumed 59.5% = 517 of 869). OCR noted limitations and conservative assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory policies and effects (contract standard §438.3(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: MCOs, PIHPs, PAHPs, PCCMs and similar entities will not discriminate against individuals eligible to enroll on the basis of race; color; national origin; disability; or sex (which includes sex characteristics, intersex traits, pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes), and will not use any policy or practice that has the effect of discriminating on these bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition covers both intentional discrimination and policies/practices that have discriminatory effects. This standard is incorporated into standard contract requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access and cultural competence requirement for managed care (§438.206(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP participates in the State's efforts to promote the delivery of services in a culturally competent manner to all enrollees, including those with limited English proficiency and diverse cultural and ethnic backgrounds, disabilities, and regardless of sex (including sex characteristics, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, sex stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in state efforts is required to promote culturally competent delivery; this is intended to ensure services meet diverse needs of enrollees.

rubrics_metrics.name: State methods to promote culturally competent services (§440.262)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must have methods to promote access and delivery of services in a culturally competent manner to all beneficiaries (including LEP, diverse cultural/ethnic backgrounds, disabilities, and regardless of sex as defined), and these methods must ensure beneficiaries have access to covered services delivered in a manner that meets their individualized needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a standards-of-practice expectation for States to implement methods that ensure individualized, culturally competent care across beneficiary populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of culturally competent access requirement in state assurances (§457.495(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: State assurances regarding access to care and procedures to assure quality and appropriateness of care must include access to and delivery of services in a culturally competent manner as described in 42 CFR 440.262.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties State grant/allotment assurances to the culturally competent delivery requirement found in §440.262.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination via decision support tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule prohibits discrimination through the use of decision support tools; discriminatory application of decision support tools (e.g., incorrect diagnoses for patients of certain races) can lead to delayed or denied care and negative health outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR highlights both harms of discriminatory decision support use and potential benefits of unbiased tools (e.g., earlier identification of cardiovascular risk). The rule aims to prevent discriminatory algorithmic or tool-based practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of process for religious/conscience exemption requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department includes a process for covered entities to submit requests for assurance of a religious or conscience-based exemption rather than excluding such a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR estimated that excluding the exemption process would reduce quantified costs but rejected that alternative due to obligations to enforce federal religious freedom and conscience laws and commitment to provide a clear administrative process that respects objections while protecting patients' rights and health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for considering demographic data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department considered requiring covered entities to collect self-identified race, ethnicity, primary language (spoken and written), sex (consistent with §92.101(a)(2)), age, and disability status but concluded existing authorities (section 1557, title VI, section 504, title IX, Age Act) already provide ability to collect such data for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department weighed authority, utility for compliance monitoring, and did not finalize a new mandatory universal data-collection requirement in this rulemaking.
